questions.question: Which MIR196A genomic locus showed the clear precursor-RNA response to estradiol in MCF7 cells?

options.A: MIR196A2 at the HOXC locus, not MIR196A1.
options.B: MIR196A1 at the HOXB locus, not MIR196A2.
options.D: Neither locus responded; only mature miRNA changed.

questions.rationale: The transcriptional induction was assigned to MIR196A2; the report explicitly contrasts it with unresponsive MIR196A1.
questions.evidence_quote: These data clearly indicate an increase in precursor miRNA from MIR196A2 but not MIR196A1 in response to E2. Taken together this suggests that MIR196A2 is transcriptionally regulated by oestrogen.

questions.question: When did nascent RNA production around MIR196A2 peak after estradiol addition?
questions.rationale: GRO-Seq showed a rapid, transient transcriptional response with its maximum around 40 minutes.
questions.evidence_quote: Global-run-on sequencing (GRO-Seq) is able to measure nascent RNA, assessing changes in transcription with high sensitivity. Analysis of MCF7 GRO-Seq data clearly indicates a dramatic increase in RNA production in the genomic region surrounding MIR196A2, peaking at 40 mins following addition of oestradiol (E2)

questions.question: Which promoter was most active in the MCF7 luciferase assay among the tested putative promoters?

options.A: PP1, corresponding to the HOXC10 promoter.
options.B: PP2, corresponding to the HOTAIR enhancer.
options.D: All three promoters were equally active.

questions.rationale: PP1 drove the strongest reporter activity; PP2 had only modest activity and PP3 was not active in this assay.
questions.evidence_quote: Upon cloning of these putative promoter sites into luciferase reporter vectors where PP1 and also PP2; modestly; increases luciferase gene transcription (Figure 1E ), with the most active promoter in MCF7 cells, PP1 (HOXC10 promoter).

questions.question: Which distal regulatory elements were identified as interacting with MIR196A2 promoters?

options.A: The previously known HOTAIR distal enhancer (HDE) and a novel MIR196A2 enhancer (mE).
options.B: Two HOXB9 promoters, PP1 and PP3.

questions.rationale: ChIA-PET identified the known HDE and a new interacting partner called mE.
questions.evidence_quote: One of these is a previously identified HOTAIR enhancer (HOTAIR distal enhancer, HDE (15) ) and the other a novel interacting partner (MIR196A2-Enhancer, mE).

questions.question: In which breast cancer subtype did high MIR196A expression associate with better outcome?
questions.rationale: In contrast with ER+ disease, high MIR196A was associated with better outcome in TNBC.
questions.evidence_quote: whilst high expression associates with a better outcome in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC)

questions.question: Among ER+ patients responding to hormone therapy and chemotherapy, what 10-year survival figures distinguished low- and high-MIR196A groups?

options.A: More than 95% for low expression versus 61% for high expression.
options.B: 61% for low expression versus more than 95% for high expression.

questions.rationale: Low-expression patients had very high 10-year survival; the high-expression cohort had substantially worse survival.
questions.evidence_quote: Women with low MIR196A expression had exhibited a high rate of survival (>95% at 10 years), whilst most women within the high expression group died within 17 years (61% at 10 years).

questions.question: How did menopause modify the prognostic direction of MIR196A in ER+ disease?

options.A: High expression was associated with good outcome before menopause but poor outcome after menopause.
options.B: High expression was associated with poor outcome before menopause but good outcome after menopause.
options.C: MIR196A was prognostic only in premenopausal women, always favorably.
options.D: Menopause did not alter the association.

questions.rationale: The paper reports a reversal by menopausal status, cautioning against treating MIR196A as a uniform prognostic marker.
questions.evidence_quote: In premenopausal women, high expression of MIR196A is associated with a good outcome in ER+ disease (Table 1 ). Multivariate analysis demonstrates that MIR196A is one of the few significant biomarkers for ER+ tumours arising before menopause. In post-menopausal women, all tested biomarkers were significant in ER+ disease, including MIR196A, however high expression is now associated with a poor outcome.

questions.question: How did MIR196A expression differ between tamoxifen-resistant and fulvestrant-resistant MCF7 models?

options.A: It increased in TAMR cells but was nearly depleted in FASR cells.
options.B: It was nearly depleted in TAMR but increased in FASR.
options.C: It increased equally in both resistant models.
options.D: It was unchanged in both models.

questions.rationale: The resistance models showed divergent MIR196A expression, rather than a generic increase under all endocrine resistance.
questions.evidence_quote: Using established models of HR+ disease resistance we found that MIR196A expression is significantly increased in tamoxifen resistant MCF7 cells (TAMR) whilst it is almost depleted in fulvestrant resistance (FASR)

questions.question: What evidence linked altered MIR196A expression to chemotherapeutic resistance in cell-line models?

options.A: MIR196A increased in paclitaxel- and adriamycin-resistant lines relative to treatment-sensitive cells.
options.B: MIR196A decreased in all resistant lines relative to sensitive cells.
options.C: Only paclitaxel resistance altered MIR196A, while adriamycin had no effect.
options.D: Resistance increased MIR196A only in patient metastases, not cell lines.

questions.rationale: The authors report increased expression in models resistant to both listed chemotherapeutic agents.
questions.evidence_quote: Using RNA-Seq data for cell line models of resistance to paclitaxel and adromycin, two common chemotherapeutics, MIR196A expression again increases in resistant cell lines compared to the treatment sensitive cell line

questions.question: What central evidence limitation did the authors identify about interpreting MIR196A’s role in therapeutic resistance?

options.A: It remained unclear whether increased MIR196A is required for resistance or merely accompanies it.
options.B: The study proved MIR196A alone causes all forms of resistance.
options.C: The study lacked any resistant cell models.
options.D: Only normal tissue was profiled, so no cancer inference was possible.

questions.rationale: The paper presents MIR196A as a possible biomarker and explicitly calls for functional studies to determine whether it is causative or cooperative.
questions.evidence_quote: This miRNA is a possible biomarker for the progression of breast tumour to becoming resistant to therapy. Future studies should aim to uncover the purpose of increase MIR196A expression and if it is required for development of resistance alone or in combination with other HOXC genes.
